name: Alpha-ketoglutarate

lead: Alpha-ketoglutarate (AKG) is a key intermediate in the citric acid cycle and in amino acid metabolism. It is sold as a supplement, often as calcium AKG.

It attracted longevity interest after mouse studies showed extended lifespan and compressed morbidity. Human evidence is preliminary, with small, company-linked studies and no demonstrated cosmetic benefit.

paras: AKG is a cofactor for dioxygenases involved in epigenetic regulation (such as TET enzymes and histone demethylases) and for collagen hydroxylation, and it links energy and nitrogen metabolism.

Generally regarded as well tolerated in short-term use, but long-term human safety data are limited. Legal as a supplement. Claims about reduced biological age come from small, non-definitive studies.
